notes: The engine against the servers it is measured by, on the same GGUF, the same GCD, the same
KV pool, slots and cache types: llama-server built from the engine's own llama.cpp commit
without EuLLM's patches (the difference is EuLLM's runtime: scheduler, batching, API) and
Ollama, the API EuLLM is compatible with. Objective (2), and the reference frame for (1).
Binaries: tools/lumi/install_runtimes.sh (llama-server built here, Ollama's latest release
with its ROCm libraries, its models made from the EuLLM store's GGUFs).
vLLM is not here yet: it serves Hugging Face weights rather than GGUF, so it needs its own
like-for-like design, and its ROCm container has to be shown to run on gfx90a first.
Catalog models (Q4_K_M), already in the store for c01.
rt-kvu*: EuLLM alone, a KV cache per slot (its default) against one for all (--kv-unified),
side by side in each group. On one GCD with Qwen3-14B (job 22691743, 10-10-2026) one cache
for all was 9% faster with 16 clients sending requests one after another (no gaps in the
slots' run, no passes of their own for the prompts) and 7% slower with 16 at once (each
answer's attention reads every slot's cells), a cost that grows with the context. These
points decide whether --kv-unified becomes the default above one slot.
